rationale: The PubMed abstracts consistently show that changes in triglyceride levels are associated with changes in HDL cholesterol, supporting a relationship between these entities. PMID 17351155 demonstrates that reducing triglycerides (via orlistat) was associated with changes in HDL-C levels. PMID 25726220 shows triglycerides and HDL cholesterol as related metabolic syndrome components. While INDRA provides no directional statements, the clinical literature pattern suggests triglycerides influence HDL (the proposed direction), as interventions targeting triglycerides tend to affect HDL levels, and hypertriglyceridemia is known to lower HDL through mechanisms like CETP activity.
search_query: (Triglycerides -- blood fat level (lipid panel).) AND (HDL ('good') cholesterol (lipid panel).)
